name: the

phase_0.boundary_condition: the noun phrase bound by the definiteness marker

VINIT.justification: The initial state before any definite reference is attempted; no referent has been selected or fixed.

TANCH.justification: The article itself closes the referent into a bounded unique entity, acting as the terminal anchor of the referential act.

AFWD.justification: Forward morphism from the set of possible referents to the uniquely identified one via prior mention or situation.

AREV.justification: Reverse morphism from the selected referent back to the discourse context that established its uniqueness.

CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining of the definite article with the nominal predicate and the discourse history that identifies the referent.

IMSCRIB.justification: The referent is recognized as itself across mentions; the article asserts that the designated entity is identical to the already-introduced one.

FSPLIT.justification: Splits the discourse into two branches: (1) the referent is already present in discourse memory, (2) the referent is uniquely inferable from the situational context without prior mention.

FFUSE.justification: Reconstitutes the two identification paths into a single definite noun phrase that carries the uniqueness property, recovering the input condition of a pending referent.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative branch where the referent matches a previously introduced entity; the article functions as a pure anaphora.

EVALF.justification: Negative branch (in evaluation sense) where the referent is not in memory but is uniquely given by the extra-linguistic context (e.g., 'the sun').

ENGAGR.justification: Both anaphoric and situational sources apply simultaneously, as when a referent is accessed via a related entity in memory while also being contextually unique; the resolution is held in paradice.

IFIX.justification: Permanently records the referent identity in the discourse model, making it available for subsequent anaphoric references.

phase_2.split_input: discourse state with an unresolved referent that requires unique identification
phase_2.fuse_result: a single noun phrase that uniquely designates the referent, semantically identical to the input condition of a referent awaiting identification

phase_3.void_description: Zero referent fixed; no definite article has been processed.
phase_3.true_description: Referent uniquely identified via prior discourse mention (anaphoric).
phase_3.false_description: Referent uniquely identified via shared situational context (deictic or inferential).
phase_3.both_description: Referent is both anaphorically accessible and contextually unique (e.g., bridging reference through a related entity); held without immediate resolution.

steps.domain_action: discourse begins with no referent fixed
definite article 'the' initiates the referential boundary
evaluate source of uniqueness — anaphoric vs. situational
affirm that referent matches prior discourse entity
forward selection from memory to the exact referent
affirm that referent is uniquely available from context
reverse descent to retrieve the contextual conditions that guarantee uniqueness
merge the two branches into a single definite noun phrase
compose the article with the nominal predicate and discourse chain
assert self-identity of the referent across mentions
permanently register the referent in the discourse model

phase_5.compiler_frontend: speaker's referential intention interpreter — maps the desire to refer uniquely onto the morphosyntactic operation of article insertion
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: discourse inter-agent communication channel — enables speaker and hearer to share a referent through the article as a signal
phase_5.memory_mechanism: discourse model (a stack of referent representations with 2-step retrieval capacity, as required by the CL8NK specification)
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: utterance linearization order — determines when the article is placed relative to the noun and preceding discourse
phase_5.alfs_store: CL8NK lexicon and grammar store — provides the primitive forms (e.g., glyph sequence ⟨𐑦⋅𐑸⋅𐑾⋅𐑹⋅𐑐⋅𐑧⋅𐑲⋅𐑵⋅⊙⋅𐑫⋅𐑳⋅𐑟⟩) and the evaluation rules for definiteness

phase_6.cycle_cost: one mental token insertion per definite article use, consuming working memory for anaphoric binding
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: discourse state n with an unresolved referent, entropy H_n
phase_6.post_cycle_state: discourse state n+1 with the referent fixed and unique, entropy H_{n+1} = H_n because the referent is already determined by the previous context
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the definite article conserves discourse entropy by selecting a unique referent from an already constrained set, adding no new uncertainty
